package_info.package_versions: unknown, but affected versions distributed in late March 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp update was compromised to include malicious components (TAXHAUL loader and COLDCAT downloader), enabling remote code execution and post-installation attacks on customer systems. The attackers abused the software supply chain by injecting malware into the legitimate update process, resulting in widespread distribution of a trojanized application to downstream users.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious loader code embedded in the 3CXDesktopApp update binary that decrypts and loads shellcode (TAXHAUL), which subsequently loads a downloader (COLDCAT).
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (likely, based on Windows binary analysis)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the code decrypts embedded shellcode and executes it in memory, which then initiates a downloader to fetch additional payloads from attacker-controlled infrastructure, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of encrypted shellcode within a legitimate update binary, combined with post-installation in-memory execution, is highly indicative of malicious intent. This behavior is not consistent with standard software update practices.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate update binaries are expected to only update application files and should not contain hidden loaders or mechanisms to decrypt and execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters may download signed patches, but they do not embed or execute hidden shellcode or loaders that operate without user awareness.
key_indicators: Encrypted shellcode embedded within the update binary
Post-installation in-memory execution of decrypted payloads
Loader code present in application executable that is not part of official release
Initiation of network connections immediately after update

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloader shellcode (COLDCAT) that, once executed in memory, connects to attacker-controlled command-and-control (C2) servers and retrieves additional malicious payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the shellcode establishes outbound connections to remote C2 infrastructure, downloads further malicious payloads, and executes them in memory without user interaction, enabling continued attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The shellcode initiates unsolicited outbound network connections to unknown infrastructure and executes code fetched at runtime, which is a hallmark of malware and not expected in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not download and execute arbitrary code from the internet after installation, especially without user consent or code signing validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may fetch signed updates from trusted sources, but do not execute arbitrary shellcode or connect to untrusted C2 domains.
key_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains or IP addresses
In-memory execution of code retrieved from the internet
No user interaction required for execution of downloaded payloads
Network activity to infrastructure not associated with 3CX or its update servers

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the 3CX build/update process and injects a malicious loader (TAXHAUL) into the 3CXDesktopApp update binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious update is distributed to customer systems via the official update channel.

attack_chain.action: On customer systems, the malicious loader decrypts and executes embedded shellcode post-installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Shellcode (COLDCAT downloader) is executed in memory, preparing for further compromise.

attack_chain.action: The in-memory shellcode establishes outbound connections to attacker-controlled C2 servers and downloads additional payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-controlled code and potential further compromise of the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Post-installation execution of decrypted shellcode from update binaries
Unexpected outbound network connections initiated by update binaries or their child processes
In-memory execution of payloads not present on disk following a software update
file_indicators: 3CXDesktopApp update binaries containing embedded encrypted shellcode
Presence of anomalous loader code in application executables not matching official release signatures
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains or IP addresses as identified in threat intelligence feeds
Unusual network activity from 3CXDesktopApp or its processes immediately after update installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor update binaries for embedded encrypted payloads or unauthorized loader code using static and behavioral analysis. Detect post-installation network connections from update processes to suspicious domains or IPs. Use EDR/XDR solutions to flag in-memory execution of code not present on disk, and correlate update events with subsequent anomalous process or network activity. Cross-reference network destinations with threat intelligence to identify known C2 infrastructure.
